record.original_question: Classify the compact manifolds that admit Einstein metrics.

evidence.quote: Classify compact manifolds which admit Einstein metrics

artifact.self_contained_problem: A smooth Riemannian metric $g$ on a smooth manifold $M$ is called an Einstein metric if its Ricci curvature tensor $\mathrm{Ric}(g)$ satisfies $\mathrm{Ric}(g) = \lambda\, g$ for some constant $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$. Give a complete classification of those compact smooth manifolds $M$ (without boundary) that admit at least one Einstein Riemannian metric. More precisely, characterize, in topological or differential-topological terms, exactly which compact manifolds carry an Einstein metric, and for each such manifold describe the set (and moduli) of Einstein metrics it supports.
artifact.status_search_result: The classification of compact manifolds admitting Einstein metrics is a long-standing open problem in Riemannian geometry. Even in dimension 4, no full topological obstruction/classification is known: only partial obstructions (e.g., Hitchin–Thorpe inequality, LeBrun's Seiberg–Witten obstructions) and constructions (Kähler–Einstein, homogeneous, Sasaki–Einstein) are available. In higher dimensions the problem is essentially wide open, as discussed in Besse's monograph "Einstein Manifolds" and subsequent surveys.

status_evidence.title: Einstein Manifolds (Besse) — overview
status_evidence.snippet: Standard reference noting that the classification of compact manifolds admitting Einstein metrics is a central open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The general classification problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: C. LeBrun, Four-Manifolds without Einstein Metrics
status_evidence.snippet: Provides Seiberg–Witten obstructions to existence of Einstein metrics on 4-manifolds, indicating only partial results are known.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial obstructions exist even in dimension 4.
